propositions: Detached pytest runs via nohup report errors (leaked REPO_ROOT entries, killed browser probe) that do not reproduce in foreground runs, but detachment itself is not the cause — the cause is concurrent external mutations (file creation, process kill) that can only occur while a detached run proceeds.

The _no_repo_root_leaks guard misattributes external concurrent mutations to an innocent test, fires during teardown causing a test to report both passed and error, and silently deletes the externally-created entry.

The tests/e2e/conftest.py browser probe diagnostic fails with no message when the child process is signal-killed (returncode -9 or -15), producing an indistinguishable error from a real product failure and causing false-positive regression investigation.

A foreground suite prevents concurrent external mutation because the agent is blocked waiting; a detached suite enables it because the agent remains free to work in the checkout, making detachment an enabler rather than a root cause of the failures.

The leak guard's message must be corrected to name the possibility of external concurrent mutation rather than asserting the test caused the leak, and the e2e browser diagnostic must include proc.returncode to distinguish signal-killed children from real failures.

Documentation gap: detached-run validation practices are entirely undocumented folklore with no guidance in docs/local-dev-env.md, AGENTS.md, or CONTRIBUTING.md despite being routine practice in the project.
